source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Schedule 1 line 11 (PDF page 14); Schedule 1 line 25 (PDF page 17: 'reduced by any amounts reported on line 11'); Worksheet 2 lines 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 7a (PDF page 18); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = military retirement 15,000.00 + interest 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 30,600.00 = 85,600.00. Federal taxable income = 85,600.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500 + 2 x 1,600 age 65 or older = 34,700.00) = 50,900.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan: Schedule 1 line 11 military retirement 15,000.00 subtracted in full; line 14 Social Security 30,600.00. Older spouse born 1949 (1946-1952, past 67): Worksheet 2 line 1 40,000.00; line 2 0.00; line 3 40,000.00; line 4 active-duty pay 0.00; line 5 line-11 amount 15,000.00; line 7 = 40,000.00 - 15,000.00 = 25,000.00, Tier 2 deduction on Schedule 1 line 25 (the interest, 40,000.00, exceeds it). The retirement subtraction (Section D) would be 0.00: military retirement is not a Form 4884 benefit, so Tier 2 is the better choice. Subtractions 70,600.00. Line 14 = 85,600.00 - 70,600.00 = 15,000.00; exemptions 11,600.00; line 16 = 3,400.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 3,400.00 x 0.0425 = 144.50. No credits; state income tax 144.50.
